journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component prevents the default Tab key behavior when the popup is open, blocking focus movement to the next form field. This occurs because the Vanilla Calendar Pro (VCP) library, integrated via the datepicker component, traps focus within the popup and prevents tabbing out.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener for the Tab key on the input element when the datepicker popup is shown. This listener hides the popup, allowing the Tab key to proceed with its default focus-changing behavior. The listener is removed when the popup is hidden or the component is disposed to avoid memory leaks.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation will move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field when the datepicker popup is open, restoring expected form tab order behavior.
functional_risks: Hiding the popup on Tab key press may interrupt date selection if the user intends to tab through the calendar grid (though the calendar grid is not focusable in this implementation).
Rapid successive Tab presses may cause multiple hide/show cycles, though the _isShown flag prevents redundant operations.
The fix assumes the Tab key is the only key requiring unblocked navigation; Shift+Tab is not addressed but follows the same pattern.
If VCP internally relies on preventing Tab for its own focus management, this change could cause unexpected focus behavior within the calendar (though the calendar is not focusable in input mode).
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field when the datepicker popup is open.
Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field when the datepicker popup is closed (no regression).
Verify that pressing Escape still closes the datepicker popup (regression guard).
Verify that date selection via mouse or keyboard within the popup still functions correctly.
Verify that the popup hides when tabbing out and does not remain open.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component integrates Vanilla Calendar Pro (VCP) which, when the popup is open, sets tabindex=-1 on the input element and traps focus, preventing the Tab key from moving focus to the next form field. Additionally, VCP or the datepicker's dismiss logic calls preventDefault on the Tab keydown event, blocking the browser's default focus navigation.
plan.repair_strategy: 1. Keep the input in the tab order (tabIndex=0) while the popup is open. 2. Add a capture-phase keydown listener on the input that hides the popup on Tab key press, allowing the default focus movement to proceed. 3. Ensure the listener is added when the popup shows and removed when it hides or the component is disposed to avoid memory leaks.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab while focused on the departure date field will move focus to the passengers field, regardless of whether the datepicker popup is open. The input remains in the natural tab order, and the popup closes automatically when the user tabs out.
functional_risks: Setting tabIndex=0 may conflict with VCP's internal focus management if it expects the input to be removed from the tab order.

The capture-phase listener runs before other listeners; if VCP relies on preventing Tab in a capture listener on an ancestor, this may not fully override it (though the hide() call will still execute).
Rapid Tab presses could trigger multiple hide() calls, but the _isShown guard prevents redundant operations.
Shift+Tab is not explicitly handled but will follow the same pattern because event.key is 'Tab' for both.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field when the datepicker popup is open.
Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field when the datepicker popup is closed (no regression).
Verify that pressing Escape still closes the datepicker popup (regression guard).
Verify that date selection via mouse or keyboard within the popup still functions correctly.
Verify that the popup hides when tabbing out and does not remain open.
Verify that the departure input retains tabIndex=0 while the popup is open.
